strategies.name: support_to_resistance_scalp
strategies.entry_summary: After the first 5 to 15 minutes, identify an intraday support level on the 5-minute chart, such as the 13 EMA, the 200 EMA, or a clear demand/support area from price action. Enter when price comes down to that support and bounces from it.
strategies.exit_summary: Take profit quickly at the next resistance or after a short favorable move; the speaker repeatedly frames this as getting in at support and selling at resistance without overstaying the trade.

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: wait for the opening 5 to 15 minutes to establish support, then buy the touch/bounce of the 13 EMA
variants.target_note: exit on the quick move up / at resistance
variants.transcript_quote: this 13 EMA operated as a initial support... the stock came down and it hit right there that's our entry for a scalp

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: re-enter on a later revisit of the same support level
variants.target_note: exit after the bounce / when that move is formed
variants.transcript_quote: it came back down again boom same level you enter here and then boom you got this move now we have formed this is your exit

variants.confirmation_mechanic_note: after the 13 EMA loses support status, use the 200 EMA as deeper support and enter the bounce there
variants.target_note: ride it to resistance and exit
variants.transcript_quote: you get in here as support and you ride it to resistance and you exit okay another quick Scout this one off a deeper support sitting at the 200 EMA

result.enumeration_note: The transcript teaches one runnable long scalp skeleton: buy at established support/demand on the 5-minute chart after the open and sell quickly into resistance; the later downside move has an entry mention but only a gestural hindsight exit ('you want to exit right there'), so it is not promoted under Rule 1.
